name: Applied Physics (MS)

rules.name: Requirements Overview
rules.desc:
See Graduate Degrees for the university’s basic requirements for the master’s degree.
There are no department or university examinations. There is no thesis component. If a student is admitted to the MS program but later wishes to change to the PhD program, the student must re-apply through the admissions portal.
Only six units below the 200-level are permitted without approval by the Applied Physics Graduate Study Committee.

rules.name: Core Course Requirements (four of five areas)
rules.desc:
All Master students must complete at least one approved graduate course (for a letter grade) in each of any four of the following five areas:

• Quantum Mechanics

• Statistical and Condensed Matter Physics

• Classical Physics

• Methods

• Biophysics
A course that appears in multiple categories may be used to satisfy only one core requirement. The flagship course, offered every year by the Applied Physics department in each area is listed first (in bold). Students unfamiliar with a topic area are strongly encouraged to begin with the flagship course, or another more introductory course as needed. Discussions with the academic advisor will help students determine their appropriate curriculum. Students with prior background may choose any approved course in that category.
Complete at least 1 course in each of any 4 of the following 5 areas.
rules.notes:
Letter grade: All courses used to satisfy core requirements must be taken for a letter grade.
Double-counting: A course that appears in multiple categories may be used to satisfy only one core requirement.

rules.name: 33 units of Additional Advanced Courses in Science and/or Engineering
GPA of 3.0 (B) in the courses used for the degree

gpa: A final overall grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 (B) is for courses used to fulfill degree requirements.
grading: All courses used to satisfy the 45-unit minimum for the Master of Science degree must be taken for a letter grade if offered.
policies:
Waiver and Substitution Policy
Students with equivalent prior coursework may petition the Graduate Studies Committee for a substitution (not a waiver). Under a substitution, the student takes a different advanced course in a related area rather than skipping the requirement; the total number of required courses remains the same. Students considering a substitution should consult with their academic advisor to assess their preparation and identify an appropriate alternative course.
Petitions should include the syllabus and transcript from the prior course. The committee chair reviews for equivalency.
Outright waivers (reducing the number of courses) are granted only in rare circumstances.
transferPolicy: All coursework for the Applied Physics MS degree must be completed through Stanford.
reviewNotes: The audit checks one letter-graded core course in each of any four of the five areas (a course counts for one area only) and 33 more units from APPPHYS 290, the listed seminars and the listed advanced courses. Every course toward the 45 units must be letter graded when that option is offered, and at most six units below the 200 level count. Seminars or other courses your advisor approves are moved in by hand, and you check the 3.0 GPA by hand.
